summary: A guide to Reiki and Qigong as energy healing practices used as adjuncts to conventional medicine. It explains their origins, how to learn and practice each, cited research on benefits, tips for getting started, and their growing presence in mainstream healthcare. It stresses consulting healthcare professionals and keeping realistic expectations.
one_line: Guide to Reiki and Qigong covering origins, learning paths, daily practice, research on wellness benefits, and integration into mainstream healthcare.
key_facts: Reiki was developed in early 20th century Japan by Mikao Usui and works by a therapist channeling energy through touch or close proximity.
Qigong is an ancient Chinese practice combining movement, meditation, and controlled breathing to cultivate and balance qi, or life force energy.
Reiki is taught in a lineage from master to student and requires attunements or initiations.
Reiki education has three levels: self-healing and close-proximity healing, distance healing, and becoming a Reiki Master who can teach and attune others.
A self-Reiki practice can take as little as 15 minutes a day, placing hands on different parts of the body.
Qigong needs no specific initiation, suits all ages, and can be adapted for people with limited mobility.
Qigong exercises can range from five minutes to an hour; morning sessions refresh the mind and evening sessions help unwind.
Jane Smith is described as a certified Reiki master since 2025 who hosts workshops throughout the year in the area.
David Lee is a Qigong expert described as teaching since 2027.
A June 2024 study led by Dr. Carlos Garcia at the University of Miami reported significant improvements in quality of life scores for patients receiving Reiki alongside conventional cancer treatment.
A study published in October 2025 by the National Institute of Complementary Medicine found regular Qigong practitioners had lowered blood pressure and heart rate.
The note advises always consulting healthcare professionals before using integrative or alternative practices, especially with existing medical conditions.
Hospitals are incorporating Reiki for patient care, and corporate wellness programs increasingly offer Qigong classes to reduce workplace stress.
The Global Energy Healing Conference is slated for Spring 2026 as a venue for workshops and retreats.
